results.summary_before: This design implements a single neuron in a binarized neural network (BNN), performing binary multiplication with XNOR, accumulation, and sign activation. It simulates the behavior of a neuron by accumulating XNOR results and applying a sign function to output +1 or -1. The design is tested by resetting the circuit and providing constant inputs and weights with an enable signal to begin the XNOR multiplication. It is a demonstration of BNN concepts and requires no external hardware.

results.summary_before: This design is an 8-bit wide, 128-byte ROM containing information about the Tiny Tapeout chip, including the shuttle name and commit hash in 7-segment encoding and an ASCII chip descriptor string. The contents are read by setting the 8-bit address on the input pins and observing the data on the output pins, with the first bytes viewable on an on-board seven-segment display. The ROM is automatically generated by the tt-support-tools during GDS build. It is a utility design for chip identification rather than a computational block.

results.summary_before: This design implements two leaky integrate-and-fire neurons and a spike-timing dependent plasticity module that updates a synaptic weight based on the timing difference between pre- and post-synaptic spikes. A drive current is applied to the neuron and integrated every clock cycle, with the LIF spike, LIF state, and synaptic weight brought out as outputs. The documentation describes the learning rule and testing procedure at a high level. It is a compact hardware demonstration of a biologically inspired learning mechanism.
